description:
FILED s473t5f (#1501 round 7, uni/, 2026-09-13).  PRE-EXISTING; ASCII-probed,
so it is not a Unicode matter at all.

`caller`'s 4th and 5th list elements -- `subroutine` (index 3) and `hasargs`
(index 4) -- are incomplete:

  * an ANONYMOUS sub reports UNDEF where perl reports `PKG::__ANON__`;
  * a DELETED sub (its GV removed from the stash) keeps reporting its OLD
    NAME where perl reports `__ANON__` -- perl anonymises a CV that was
    relying on a real GV for its name;
  * a frame whose caller is an `eval {}` or `eval ''` reports UNDEF where
    perl reports the ENCLOSING SUB's name;
  * `hasargs` is ALWAYS undef; perl gives 1 for every ordinary sub call.

PROBE (scratch/s473t5f/probes/caller-fields.pl; perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):

                        perl                        PCL
  anon          name='Main2::__ANON__' hasargs=1    name=undef        hasargs=undef
  deleted       name='Main2::__ANON__' hasargs=1    name='Main2::foo' hasargs=undef
  caller(1)     name='Main2::outer'    hasargs=1    name='Main2::outer' hasargs=undef
  eval-block    name='Main2::inev'     hasargs=1    name=undef        hasargs=undef
  eval-string   name='Main2::inevs'    hasargs=1    name=undef        hasargs=undef

So the NAME is right for an ordinary named call and wrong for the three
special frames; `hasargs` is never set at all.

WHAT IT COSTS: `t/uni/caller.t` -- ALL 12 of its blessed fail rows plus the
one `*extra*` row, i.e. the whole file's residue.  t/op/caller.t is the ASCII
twin and will have the same cluster.

NOT COVERED BY THE EXISTING NOT-SUPPORTED ENTRY: `docs/not-supported.md`
"`caller()` filename and line number [DEFERRED]" is about elements 1 and 2
(filename, line).  Elements 3 and 4 are a different question and PCL already
maintains a per-sub caller stack for element 0 (see
`docs/caller-implementation.md`), so this is a matter of what that stack
records, not of source positions.

FIX SHAPE: `docs/caller-implementation.md` describes the dynamic
`*pcl-current-package*` + per-sub caller stack.  `hasargs` is a constant 1 for
a sub call and 0 for an eval frame -- free.  `__ANON__` needs the p-sub frame
to carry whether the sub has a NAME, and the deleted-sub case needs the name
looked up at CALL time rather than baked in, which is the same question
#1664's typeglob model asks.  Do `hasargs` first: it is one slot and four of
the twelve rows.
subject: caller() elements 3 and 4: an anonymous sub reports undef (perl: PKG::__ANON__), a deleted sub keeps its old name, an eval frame reports undef, and hasargs is ALWAYS undef -- all 12 rows of t/uni/caller.t
